definition: Evaluate Uncalled4 as a fast and accurate toolkit for nanopore signal-to-reference alignment enabling modification detection
assumptions: Pore model k-mer parameters are pre-trained and normalized
m6A predictions are generated by m6Anet using signal alignments from each tool
Ground truth labels are derived from GLORI or m6A-Atlas databases
Performance benchmarks are measured on comparable hardware
invariants: Same m6Anet model used for both Uncalled4 and Nanopolish predictions
Same reference genome/transcriptome used for all tools
Same set of candidate sites evaluated for m6A detection
structural_steps: 1. Benchmark alignment speed and file size across 4 chemistries and 4 tools
2. Analyze pore model k-mer parameters (current mean, std, dwell time)
3. Compute substitution profiles to understand base-position effects
4. Evaluate m6A detection using precision-recall and ROC analysis
5. Compare Uncalled4 vs Nanopolish alignment quality via downstream m6A calling
deviations: Analysis uses pre-computed pore models and predictions rather than running the full pipeline
Cannot reproduce the actual signal alignment step (requires FAST5/POD5 files)
